title: Systematic review of studies using platelet serotonin content to assess bioeffect of serotonin reuptake inhibitors at the serotonin transporter
population: Published studies measuring platelet serotonin content before and after starting SSRIs or SNRIs in patients and healthy volunteers
funder: not stated: the archived publisher page shows ethics declarations without a funding statement.
authorConflicts: Anderson reported personal fees from the University of Pennsylvania, Columbia University, King's College, Novartis, Neurogen and Eli Lilly.
result: Clinical doses of serotonin reuptake inhibitors typically reduced platelet serotonin content by 70% to 90%, similarly across SSRIs and SNRIs, consistent with brain SERT occupancy from neuroimaging and with in vitro platelet uptake inhibition. Results read from the abstract.
